reason: Revision of the five questions judged 'revise' in the first review (op-threshold-block, op-tie-block-transport, op-layer-period, op-continuum-ties-blocks, op-deformation-boundary). Topics are unchanged. Each statement now carries the status and range that the published records actually give (proved / certified / informal / observed / heuristic / open), the premises that the review found contradicted by the records are restricted to the regimes or parameters where the records show them, the two length scales k^(2/3) and k^(1/3) are kept apart, and every question ends with an explicit sufficiency criterion and a one-sentence boundary against the neighbouring questions (including the two admitted ones, op-central-window and op-left-right-asymmetry). Record coordinates are those of the instance at frontier revision 184; the right half is informally proved and the left interior is what remains of the root.

questions.statement: In four regimes the records show the one-step difference d = b_{n,k} - b_{n,k-1} decided at a relative margin of order k^(-1/3): the centre t = (n-2k)/k^(2/3) -> 0, where the two compared terms share their leading constant and differ by (2/I_0) k^(-1/3) (I_0 = Gamma(2/3)/3^(1/3)); the first layer at fixed lambda = k/n in (1/2,1), where the margin is (m(lambda)+o(1)) k^(-1/3) (informal proof); the second layer lambda in (1/3,1/2), where the predicted margin is m_3(lambda) k^(-1/3) with min m_3 ~ 15.34 (conjecture with measurements); and the right critical window at finite c, where the margin falls short of its universal limit by D(x-hat) c^(-1/3), D ~ 5-9.5 (observation). In the first layer (informal proof) and conjecturally in the second, the mechanism is a rare cluster of k^(1/3) heavy sites carried by one component that lands within O(k^(2/3)) above the capacity k, set against a smooth background curvature that stays O(1): the convex-kink identity d = Conv - Kink shows that the moment test measures two pieces of amplitude D I_0 k^(1/3) whose difference is the finite layer curvature. Two other regimes look different in the records and are not assumed to share this premise: inside the central window at fixed t in [t_0,T] the moment ratio converges to a k-independent profile R_inf(t) (maximum ~2.25 at t ~ 4) and the margin is O(1), and in the pole regime n >> k^(3/2) the mean E[Z] ~ kappa_k n grows linearly so that E^2 dominates the other moment terms, while the concentrated blocks are prime blocks of size just BELOW k, in a boundary layer of width k/sigma_k; no k^(1/3) heavy-site mass and no k^(-1/3) margin is shown there. The question: what is the local limit law of the threshold-adjacent component in the k^(-1/3) regimes - the law of its size offset above k (scale k^(2/3)), of its heavy-site count (scale k^(1/3)), of its tie/blocked status, and of its first finite-size correction - and is it one and the same object at the centre, in the first layer, in the second layer and in the right window, with only the macroscopic intensity (B_lambda + D_lambda in the first layer, the boundary flux D_3 in the second) changing? Two scales inside the cluster must be kept apart: the cluster sits at stopping depth O(k^(2/3)) above k (92-95% of the blocked-maximum loss comes from chains that descended to within 0.5 k^(2/3) of k), while the gain/loss boundary in chain-endpoint distance is a band of the narrower scale k^(1/3) (heuristically r* ~ 0.63 k^(1/3)); a local law must resolve both. A sufficient answer gives one local law from which the regime constants 2/I_0 (centre), m(lambda) and m_3(lambda) (layers) and D(x-hat) (right window) are recovered, and states whether the window-interior object (two components, O(1) margin) and the pole-regime boundary-layer block are the same local object seen under different intensities or genuinely different objects; or it shows that the k^(-1/3) regimes themselves involve different local objects. Boundary: op-central-window asks for the t-profiles and the landmark coincidence of the window; op-layer-period asks for the macroscopic constants kappa_r, D_r, m_r and their hand-over to the pole regime; op-continuum-ties-blocks asks for the continuum identification of ties and blocks in the right window; this question asks only whether the threshold-local object is shared.

Regimes that differ: r6b37c7e... section 6.6 - R converges to R_inf(t), maximum ~2.25 at t ~ 4, 1 as t -> 0; for t in [t_0,T] the relative margin stays O(1), k-independent; the limit function was not derived; r10ff8c2... section 5.1 - in the pole regime n >> k^(3/2), E ~ kappa_k n and E^2 dominates the other terms; rf451d83... sections 3.1-3.3 - the prime-length law has a body n <= k with factor e^(sigma_k n/k) that concentrates mass in a boundary layer of width ~k/sigma_k just below k (the tail n > k has mass 0.18 -> 0.14), a period-k oscillation through the second zero pair, and a resonance trough at k*theta ~ 2 pi of depth ~1.5/sigma_k (observations); nothing there shows a component just above k, k^(1/3) heavy-site mass, or a k^(-1/3) margin. Two scales: ra52a3c0... section 5 - 92-95% of kE[H_k] comes from chains that descended to within k + 0.5 k^(2/3) (stopping depth; producer's heuristic picture; D* = 0.542 k^(2/3)); r20df549... section 3.5 Lemma 3.2 (proved: hazard h_pi(r) -> beta_r/(e - sum_{j<r} beta_j), 1/e at r = 0) and section 3.6b (r* ~ 0.63 k^(1/3) is a heuristic prediction of the depth-law model; observed r* = 1, 4, 8, 13). The k^(2/3) stopping depth and the k^(1/3) endpoint band are different scales. The index module large-subtree-path-and-borel-renewal insists that the global chains (maximum-tree chain, nested block path, late-maximum chain, prime renewal) are different processes; this question presupposes that distinction and asks about local structure only. Conjectural.

questions.statement: The one-step difference is a difference of two positive counts, b_{n,k} - b_{n,k-1} = 2E_{n,k} - B_{n,k-1} (even ties at the maximum minus blocked maxima), of the same order and with relative gap of order n^(-1/3) in the right bulk. On the right half (k+1 <= n <= 2k-1) an exact decomposition by chain endpoint is proved, and the sign of each endpoint class is the comparison of two quantities: a hazard - the probability that the forest under an endpoint at distance r above k contains a tree of size exactly k - which converges (proved) to h_pi(r) with h_pi(0) = 1/e and h_pi(r) ~ 1/(2r), against the class's tie gain g ~ E[N(N-1)]/k. From this, large-n computations (binary64, lambda in {0.6, 0.7, 0.8}, n <= 3*10^4) show a three-stage sign -,+,- by endpoint: chains ending within r*(k) of the threshold lose, chains ending somewhat further gain, shallow chains lose; r* = 1, 4, 8, 13 at n = 600, 3000, 10^4, 3*10^4 (lambda = 0.7), the deep-class loss is certified exactly at (n,k) = (300,210), (600,420), (1000,700), and a depth-law model built on the published Palm law predicts r* ~ 0.63 k^(1/3) heuristically (the needed upper bound on the endpoint-conditioned pair count is unproved). At small n (<= 110) most increasing positions are instead +- (1277 of 1610), so the three-stage shape is a large-n phenomenon. Slicing by H_k, the h = 0 slice is always >= 0 while h >= 1 slices turn negative well before the mode, and the site-wise comparison already fails at site k: the positivity is a global compensation that no H-preserving slice-wise or site-wise injection can exhibit. Where does the compensation live? (i) Is there a pairing or transport that carries blocked-maximum mass to tie mass between endpoint classes - in the narrowest sense one that changes only the last step of the same chain (endpoint displacement O(1) or o(k^(1/3))), in a wider sense one whose endpoint displacement is O(k^(1/3)), the width of the loss band - or must any transport that accounts for the sign move mass across endpoint distances >> k^(1/3) or between different global structures (non-local)? (ii) How close to a bijection must it be - the relative gap is n^(-1/3), so asymptotically almost bijective - and does that exclude every argument that loses a constant factor locally? (iii) What replaces the chain-endpoint classes on the left half (n > 2k), where the vertices of size > k form a tree with side branches and H_k can exceed 1: is there a leaf-wise decomposition with the same two-ingredient sign test? A sufficient answer exhibits an explicit transport in one of the senses of (i) that accounts for the sign geography on the right (the three-stage shape and the growth of r*), or proves that no transport with endpoint displacement O(k^(1/3)) exists; and gives, or rules out, the leaf-wise analogue on the left. Boundary: op-left-right-asymmetry asks which structural feature separates the two halves and whether the right-side unconditioning device has a left analogue; this question asks for the combinatorial pairing behind the sign and its left-half form.

section 3.4: class sign D(m) > 0 iff g(m) > Psi_k(m)/Phi_k(m); section 3.5 Lemma 3.2 (proved): Psi_k(k+r)/Phi_k(k+r) -> h_pi(r) = beta_r/(e - sum_{j<r} beta_j), h_pi(0) = 1/e, h_pi(1) = 0.2141, h_pi(r) ~ 1/(2r); section 5.1: the relative gap of 2E >= B is n^(-1/3) (published profile h_cmp); section 7: open questions - inter-class transport ('pairing the loss of chains ending within r* with the gain class obtained by altering the same chain's last step'), the pairing must be asymptotically almost bijective, and the left-half generalisation to a leaf-wise decomposition was not attempted. ra52a3c0... section 6 and review/feedback.md section 5.2: the h = 0 slice is always >= 0; h >= 1 slices are negative well before the mode (the review corrects the n = 25 figure: the h = 1 slice is negative for k >= 10, some h >= 1 slice for every 2 <= k <= 24); the Z <= 1 slice is always <= 0; the site-wise comparison fails at i = k; the review reads the conclusion as 'impossible by H-preserving slice-wise or site-wise comparison'. r475ada... section 7 item 3: on the left the loss of the published bound is entirely in B <= J^G, and beyond the band the right comparison is 'excess of K'' versus excess of B', two negative quantities that nearly cancel. r9d97cea... section 8.2: for n > 2k heavy sites acquire active side branches; the restricted response has an exact recursion (Theorem R1) but its asymptotics are open. The transport itself is conjectural.

questions.statement: The left half is organised by the number r ~ n/k of components above capacity, and the records establish the layer structure unevenly in r. The fixed-ratio profiles Phi_r and their strict convexity are proved. The normalised curvature M_r = Phi_r''/Phi_r has an interior minimum at lambda*_2 = 0.6435 (closed form) and lambda*_3 = 0.4240 (interval-certified); lambda*_4 ~ 0.308 is a numerical value and the interior minimum for r = 4 rests on a heuristic local analysis (M_4 diverges like eps^(-3/2) at the upper end); for r >= 5 it is unknown whether M_r has an interior minimum, and for r >= 6 the upper-end singularity of Phi_r may be bounded, so the endpoint argument need not apply. Accordingly the mechanism 'each layer sits between a block-is-born threshold and a block-disappears threshold, so mu = d/A cannot be monotone inside it' is established for r = 2, 3 (Theorem B, informal, from published inputs), conditional on numerics for r = 4, and open beyond. The layer constants - curvature kappa_r = lambda^2 Phi_r''/Phi_r, boundary flux D_r (the cluster intensity), and the moment-margin constant m_r = kappa_r/(D_r I_0) - are known for r = 2 (closed form m(lambda), finite 2/I_0 at the centre) and r = 3 (conjecture with measurements; the end-of-layer constants 9/(8 I_0) and 1/(3 I_0) and an exponent rule are proved; interior minimum ~15.34 at n/k ~ 2.55), and have not been treated for r >= 4 or for r growing with k, although the open columns 2001 <= k <= 9949 start at n/k >= 2.01 and belong to these higher layers. Along n the moment statistics E_n, T_n, P_k(n) oscillate with period about k and T_n decreases on long intervals (so n-monotonicity reductions are false); in the pole regime n >> k^(3/2) the same period-k structure reappears as the second zero pair of the prime-block renewal, whose gap delta* sigma_k^2 = 33-47 at k <= 10^5 is still far from the asymptotic 2 pi^2, and the mean matches the one-pole formula (N/k) kappa_k - 1 with the logarithmic growth of E[Z] confined to the cell j/k in [1, 1.25). The question: how do kappa_r, D_r, m_r behave for r >= 4 and uniformly as r grows with k - in particular, do M_r and m_r keep an interior minimum and does the k^(-1/3) margin scale persist when the upper-end singularity of Phi_r weakens (r >= 6), and does the first-layer cluster law with boundary-flux intensity carry over layer by layer - and how does the layer description hand over to the renewal description with slope kappa_k and threshold density P_k(infinity)? A sufficient answer gives formulas or asymptotics for kappa_r, D_r, m_r valid uniformly in r, settles the existence of interior minima of M_r and m_r for r >= 4 (at least deciding r = 4 rigorously), and matches the layer constants to the pole-regime quantities kappa_k, P_k(infinity) and the period-k oscillation; or it shows that the hand-over is not uniform and locates where it breaks. Boundary: op-threshold-block asks whether the threshold-local object is the same across regimes; this question asks for the macroscopic layer constants and the r -> infinity hand-over.

questions.statement: In the right critical window x = (n-k)/n^(2/3) the two positive counts in b_{n,k} - b_{n,k-1} = 2E_{n,k} - B_{n,k-1} have conjectured universal limits: Theorem C (informal outline, not written out) gives c^(4/3) B_{n,c-1}/p_n -> B-hat(x-hat)/(2 pi) and c^(4/3) e_n/p_n -> E-hat(x-hat)/pi for the two-tie count e_n, and numerically (2 E-hat - B-hat)/(2 pi) = -f' where f is the published limit density of the normalised deficit: the slope of the critical density is 'two-car tie density minus blocked-maximum density', and the mode x_* = 0.5996 is where the two densities balance (the zero of the limit margin is x-hat_0 = 0.59963, equal to x_* to four digits). Two things are already known about this identity. From the published third-order local limits, c^(4/3) (V - B)/p_n -> -f' holds for V = 2E (all even ties), so, given Theorem C, the identity is equivalent to the statement that four or more cars tying at the maximum are negligible on the window scale. And a heuristic identification - threshold sites (capacity exactly k) <-> the increments dR of the Brownian running maximum R, with q_j dx = E[R^j e^(-Lambda) dR]/j! - reproduces the mode-constant limits lim eps_c = -0.29710, lim E[Z_c H_c] = 0.44299, lim F_c = 0.14589, with which the measured values (n = 200 ... 20000) are compatible, moving toward them for n >= 1000 though not monotonically. What is asked beyond this reduction: which events of (R, Lambda) are 'two cars tie at the maximum' and 'the maximum is blocked by capacity', so that E-hat and B-hat are identified as functionals of (R, Lambda) and Theorem C, the identity and the mode-constant limits follow from the continuum law rather than from numerics? A sufficient answer (a) proves Theorem C or otherwise identifies E-hat and B-hat as functionals of (R, Lambda); (b) proves the threshold-site <-> dR identification and the interchange of window limits with differences that the mode-constant computation uses; (c) reconciles E-hat, B-hat with the existing continuum functions of the boundary comparisons, H_S = -2[h_2 f'' + 3 h_3 f'] and H_C = 2 h_2 h_2' - 3 h_3 f' (H_S = 2 H_C - 2 h_2 q_0'); and (d) says what the same event identification gives in the central window where two components contribute (S = X^(1) + X^(2)). Boundary: op-central-window asks for the t-profiles and the landmark coincidence of the central window; op-threshold-block asks whether the threshold-local object is shared across regimes; this question asks only for the continuum identification of the two counts.

Its review (feedback.md section 5.1; assessment claim mode-constant-limits) corrects the record's 'monotone' wording: e_c/n^(1/3) runs 0.5521 -> 0.5476 -> 0.5488 (limit 0.5507) and eps_c runs -0.2972 -> -0.2946 -> -0.2957 (limit -0.29710), both non-monotone, E[Z_c H_c] dips slightly at n = 400, while Var Z_c, kE[H_c], -2Cov - Var H and F_c are monotone; the values are compatible with the limits and move toward them for n >= 1000, and the numerical support for lim eps_c is weaker than the record states; the claim is supported as heuristic prediction plus numerical compatibility. r5f5cf73... section 2.1 Proposition 2.1 (proved): 2E2_{n,c} - B_{n,c-1} <= b_{n,c} - b_{n,c-1}, so the node X implies that the row increases at c, and a row decrease implies that X fails; section 2.2: the converse is observed, not proved - 2E2 - B and the row difference change sign at the same integer pair for k = 500 ... 25001 and the switch tracks the row mode to second order, m + c_1 n^(-1/3) with c_1 in (1.24846, 1.24848); section 2.3 Corollary 2.4 gives this informally on the published informal quantitative expansion, and the record itself says the two are 'in effect' the same. Glossary H_S (r0dc57fa...): H_S(x) = -2[h_2 f'' + 3 h_3 f'], the limit of n^(10/3) S_{n,k}/p_n^2 for the boundary comparison; H_C (r3e8c952...): H_C = 2 q_1 h_2 - 3 h_3 q_0 = 2 h_2 h_2' - 3 h_3 f', with H_S = 2 H_C - 2 h_2 q_0'. r1b79fab... section 6: in the central window d follows (8/sqrt(pi)) f_S(t) with S = X^(1) + X^(2) in the weak sense (Proposition 2, informal). The continuum identification is conjectural.

questions.statement: Under deformations of the original object (n cars, n spaces, original arrival order, b_{n,l} = #{alpha in PF_n : M(alpha) = l}) two distinct properties have been found to fail - unimodality of a row, and decreasing-side log-concavity Q - and the deformations in the records are of three kinds. (A) Reweightings of the original row: weighting the tail coordinate r = n - l by r^a, the fixed-ratio limit density theta^a h(theta) has a dip exactly for 2 < a < a_* (a_* > 18/7, numerically ~2.5748) and for every such a the finite weighted row is eventually non-unimodal, while the exact dip at n = 304 refutes the log-tail-coordinate strengthening; the records also treat lucky-car weights x^(lucky) (x = 1 is the original row), total-displacement tilts q^T, and exponential weights t^l, for which unimodality of (t^l b_{n,l}) for all t >= 1 is reported equivalent to Q of the original row. (B) Changes of the process parameters: with n cars in n + r - 1 spaces, Q fails for all n >= 7 and r >= 64 n^3 (Theorem C) and eventually for every r_n >= n^(1+delta), but the n = 7, r = 63 row is strictly decreasing and hence unimodal: what fails there is Q, not unimodality. (C) Decompositions of the original row: fixing the outcome permutation gives a non-unimodal fibre for every n >= 7 (sigma = (1,2,3,5,4,6,7): 222 > 216 < 264 while b_7 is unimodal), and fixed preference multisets give conditional dips. For the original row itself, unimodality P is open, full log-concavity fails for all sufficiently large n (first at n = 80, l = 40), and the power-weighted limit density x^r f_X is strictly unimodal for -1/2 < r < 5/2 (proved) and non-unimodal for 5/2 < r < 5/2 + eps_0 (from the published tail expansion); nothing is settled at the endpoints or for r <= -1/2. Each record names its own cause - saturation of the independent displacement intervals in a fibre, the log-convex Cayley weight tau_m = m^(m-2)/m! of a sparse single-collision component, the polynomial tail of X - and states that it does not transfer to the original P or Q. The question: within each of the three classes, where is the boundary of the single sign change (and, separately, of Q), and is there one property of the original n-car, n-space process that every recorded failure removes and every recorded success keeps? A sufficient answer takes the recorded set - the items of (A)-(C) above, each labelled by the property that fails or survives (unimodality or Q) - and either gives a single property that separates every recorded success from every recorded failure together with the reason it holds for the original process, or proves that no single property does (two recorded failures removing different properties with no common consequence for the original row); either way it says what the statement P is really about. Boundary: the other questions ask about structure inside the original model; this one asks about its boundary under deformation.
questions.grounds: r81e7051... exposition: for sigma = (1,2,3,5,4,6,7) the fibre is (1,31,130,222,216,264,144) with 222 > 216 < 264 while b_7 = (5040,42253,62145,57398,46142,32359,16807) is unimodal; a non-unimodal fibre exists for every n >= 7; the obstacle is named saturation of the independent displacement intervals; log-concavity of the full row fails for all sufficiently large n because of the polynomial tail of X (non-explicit start), the first exact failure being n = 80, l = 40, and unimodality is verified exactly for n <= 120; limiting-shape.md section 4 (peer): x^r f_X is strictly unimodal for -1/2 < r < 5/2, and 'no conclusion is drawn here about the endpoints or outside the range'; review supported. r7eeaca03... section 6: theta^a h(theta) has a dip exactly for 2 < a < a_*, a_* = 2 + 3(1-2 theta_*)/(2(1-theta_*)(3-6 theta_*+4 theta_*^2)) > 18/7 (peer-extensions.md: numerically ~2.57480775688, the decimal not used as a premise), and for every such a all sufficiently large finite weighted rows (r^a v_n(r)) are non-unimodal; the finite dips sit at r = Theta(n), the critical structure at r = Theta(n^(2/3)), so the two results are compatible; section 7: the exact n = 304 dip 149^11 v(149)^5 > 150^11 v(150)^5 < 151^11 v(151)^5 refutes the log-tail-coordinate concavity strengthening (the unweighted counts there are decreasing, so it is no counterexample to P or Q), the rational elasticity also fails at n = 269, r = 133, and via Janson's tail expansion f_X = C x^(-5/2) + D x^(-7/2) + ... with D > 0, x^(5/2+eps) f_X is non-unimodal for all 0 < eps < eps_0; assessment supported. rd4015a8... section 6: leading coefficient a_{n,k} = C(n,k+1)(k+1)^(k-1) with ratio a_{n,k+1}^2/(a_{n,k} a_{n,k+2}) = eta_k (n-k-1)/(n-k-2), eta_k < 1 by strict log-convexity of tau_m; Theorem C (6.1): for all n >= 7, r >= 64 n^3 the row decreases at k = 1 and Q fails there (64 n^3 not claimed optimal); section 6.2: the exact n = 7, r = 63 row (19) is strictly decreasing and Q fails, with 63 the exact start for that position only; section 7: component-wise Q and reverse likelihood-ratio ordering hold for n <= 80 (observation) yet the binomial mixture violates Q; section 8: 'the original n spaces are not in this sparse regime, so this failure cannot be transferred to the original Q'; section 9 (peer): eventual Q failure for every fixed delta > 0 and r_n >= n^(1+delta); review supported. Index modules (knowledge/index/, module summaries read; the records behind them were not read in the original): weighted-shapes-and-log-coordinates - Q of the original row is equivalent to unimodality of the exponentially weighted rows (t^l b_{n,l}) for all t >= 1 (citing the 102-term record section 9), and the continuous boundary law and the finite-row obstructions are not in contradiction; lucky-weights-and-slices - b_{n,l}(x) = sum_{M=l} x^(lucky), x = 1 the original, with a weighted dip at x = n/c; total-displacement-tilts-and-geometric-endpoints - fixed 0 < q < 1 gives eventual log-convexity on every interior cell of the band c log n <= k <= D log n, and 'the Q failure for q < 1 is not a counterexample at the original q = 1'; fixed-preference-orbits-and-dickman - conditional three-term dips for all n >= 5 and q strict local peaks inside one preference multiset; surplus-spaces-and-sparse-collisions and outcome-fibres-and-saturation-obstructions - the module texts stating that these obstructions are not counterexamples to the original P or Q. The unifying account is conjectural.
